composers_checked.name: Francœur, François
composers_checked.note: Gap check (MusicBrainz works list, 78 works): no other chamber work for 3-9 players. IMSLP category holds a cello sonata and two violin sonatas (duos). The orchestral Recueil de simphonies is out of scope.

note: Slice c37: 54 works kept (29 J.C. Bach, 12 Dussek, 12 Garth, 1 Francoeur), 3 of them added because IMSLP lacks them (J.C. Bach W.B 42, W.B 60, Sextet W.B 78). Francoeur: only the E-major trio sonata (Livre II No. 12) is kept; the other 11 sonatas of the page are duos. Floor evidence: Apple Music track lists (timings), MusicBrainz, Coviello and Meridian pages, label and retailer pages; IMSLP pages read through the API. Warburton (W.B) numbers follow IMSLP and Wikipedia. Doubtful points: (1) The Nuovo Quartetto Italiano disc (Centaur) labels an Allegro/Rondo quartet "Op. 8 No. 6, W.B 56", but Coviello's W.B 56 is Andante/Minuetto (as on IMSLP), so I read the Centaur piece as W.B 60 (also recorded by Still/Perlman/Zukerman/Harrell as an oboe quartet; Il Gardellino calls it an arrangement of a string quartet): W.B 60 is kept as an oboe (or flute, violin) quartet with medium confidence: web listings (Ensemble 360, Blue Griffin) give oboe, violin, viola and cello, Bach Digital and VIAF also list a string-quartet form (Sieber Op. 14 No. 1). The Il Gardellino disc numbers Op. 11 No. 3 as W.B 73 (IMSLP and Wikipedia: W.B 72). (2) Op. 8 is recorded complete on oboe, violin, viola da gamba and cello (Coviello); entries follow the print (flute, violin, viola, cello). (3) Op. 11 bass part counted as cello (IMSLP: "or 3 violins, viola, cello"; the DG label says continuo); MusicBrainz also lists a release "Sechs Quintette Op. 11 / Zwei Sonaten Op. 16" by the Winterthurer Barock-Quintett (1981), of which I checked No. 5. (4) Op. 19 Nos. 1 and 3: third part viola per the Preston title page (IMSLP: violin or viola). (5) Keyboard: harpsichord where the print names it first (J.C. Bach Op. 2 and Op. 22, Garth), piano for J.C. Bach Op. 15 and for Dussek; harpsichord-and-strings works therefore carry the derived formation "other", as Avison does in c08. (6) Dussek Op. 68 horn is ad lib. in the Breitkopf title but the recording uses it, so it is counted as a part. Dussek Op. 37 is kept on the strength of a harp recording with violin and cello (Meridian); "harp" as an alternative to piano is not checked against the first edition. (7) IMSLP gives C. 141-143 to both the Op. 24 and Op. 29 pages; Op. 24 No. 3 is the one recorded. (8) Francoeur No. 12 is recorded with viol or cello as the obbligato bass, so cello with a viol alternative; the opus number "Op. 2" used by some labels is not used. (9) Left out as doubtful: J.C. Bach trios for two flutes and cello (W.B Inc 2, recorded by Larrieu and others; "YB 47" in MusicBrainz). The three outOfScope pages (Sinfonia concertante W.C 33, Symphony W.C 10, Francoeur Recueil de simphonies) stay out. MusicBrainz and the Divine Art page were slow or redirected at times; one Apple query for the W.B 30 trio sonata kept failing, but MusicBrainz and a web search show no recording of the W.B 30-35 trio sonatas either. Six WebSearch calls were used.
